correctness.rationale: For each zero \((i,j)\), its neighboring label sum is precisely \(R_i+C_j\). If any column is empty every row sum must be ≥2 and total weight at least \(2m\); otherwise each column has positive weight and total at least \(n\). Surjection-one placements and row-weight-two placements attain both bounds. At optimum below threshold each column has weight exactly one and all rows must occur; above threshold a zero column forces all row sums exactly two. At equality the exhaustive union has intersection counted by \((2m)!/2^m\). The direct-adjacency independent finite verifier checks all feasible labelings of total weight ≤optimum in nineteen profiles and exactly matches the formulas; finite checks are corroborative, not the proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Italian and Roman {2} are equivalent definitions, so sources using either name were compared. The complete-multipartite Roman-{2} enumerator does not imply the rook-graph count: for both factor sizes at least three, the rook graph is not complete multipartite. In the small 2-row case, the rook graph contains triangles for n≥3 and is also not generally a complete multipartite model. No accessible source states the surjection versus row-weight-two optimizer classification or its tie correction.

value.rationale: Exact classification and enumeration for an infinite natural two-parameter product-graph family identifies distinct surjection and independent row-weight-two phases, with nontrivial intersection correction at \(n=2m\). It gives the first nonzero coefficient of the Italian domination weight polynomial and precise optimizer multiplicities, sharpening but not relabeling the known square numerical result. This addresses a mathematically motivated whole-family counting problem rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
